statement: The Trichy assault rifle (TAR), sometimes known as the Tiruchi assault rifle, is an Indian-made assault rifle chambered for the 7.62×39mm round.
The TAR is based on the AR-M1, produced by Bulgarian manufacturer Arsenal AD.
Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) developed the TAR between 2011 and 2015.
Ordnance Factory Tiruchirappalli (OFT) began manufacturing TARs in 2017.
The TAR was developed to reduce dependence on imported AR-M1s under the Atmanirbhar Bharat self-reliance policy.
The TAR has been adopted by most Indian law enforcement agencies.
Prior to the TAR's introduction, India largely used foreign-made AK-style rifles.
Around 500,000 M1s were reportedly imported by India from Bulgaria in 2021 for use by the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) and Indian police forces.
As of May 2025, India is the second-largest arms importer after Ukraine, accounting for 8.3% of the arms trade, according to research data from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.
Part of the Atmanirbhar Bharat policy called for self-sufficiency to manufacture firearms in India to reduce dependence on importing small arms from other countries.
OFT announced the manufacture of an indigenous AK-based assault rifle in 2011.
The AR was named Trichy after OFT to recognise the factory's contribution in developing and manufacturing the rifle.
Some TARs were made in 2012 to be tested.
These early TARs were tested by the Border Security Force (BSF), the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), the Indo-Tibetan Border Police and the Sashastra Seema Bal.
Development started in 2015 with a production line established in 2017.
In March 2017, 200 TARs were acquired by the Chhattisgarh Police as part of the 216th Ordnance Factories Day celebration.
Concerns were raised prior to manufacture that OFT was experiencing manpower decline, leading to a decline of employees at the company.
The All India Defence Employees Federation, the Indian National Defence Workers' Federation, and the Bharatiya Pratiraksha Mazdoor Sangh stated their opposition to importing small arms.
The unions hoped that more orders for the TAR would be approved, retaining employees at OFT.
In November 2017, the CRPF conducted field tests to determine the suitability of the TAR with 15,000 rounds fired at the CRPF Academy in Kadarpur, Haryana.
There were no reports of the rifle jamming during the CRPF field tests in November 2017.
Other tests conducted included the TAR being fired from mud, rain and saltwater and from being dropped to test reliability and accuracy.
100 TARs were ordered afterwards.
In February 2018, further tests were conducted by the CRPF at Jagdalpur, Raipur, Guwahati and Srinagar.
An order of 6,167 TARs was placed afterwards in February 2018.
At the time, the CRPF tested the Trichy with the Ghatak, the Joint Venture Protective Carbine and the INSAS1C.
In March 2020, the CRPF acquired the first 500 out of 6,167 TARs sold to them.
In January 2019, the TAR was delivered to the BSF.
BSF Additional Director General Nasir Kamal received the first rifle from the Ordnance Factory Board's Director General Saurabh Kumar in January 2019.
It was reported in January 2019 that the Jharkhand Police would acquire TARs for anti-Naxalite operations.
The TAR was displayed for the first time at the Pragati Maidan in New Delhi for the 5th International Police Expo and the 4th India Homeland Security Expo.
In February 2020, the TAR was on public display at the Defence Expo at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.
It was reported at the time that the TAR was offered to the Indian Army.
OFT reported in March 2021 that around 11,500 TARs were supplied for a total of Rs 1.60 billion during fiscal year 2020–21.
In January 2021, the TriCa (Trichy Carbine) Carbine was unveiled.
Tests were conducted where 2,000 rounds were fired with no stoppages for the TriCa Carbine.
In August 2021, OFT announced that the TAR could use the ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher.
The ARDE Under Barrel Grenade Launcher was presented by OFT general manager Sanjay Dwivedi.
A TAR variant with a downfolding stock was presented publicly.
This TAR variant with a downfolding stock was sought out by the Railway Protection Force aside from the CAPFs.
In December 2021, the National Security Guard placed an order of 100 TriCa carbines.
On April 2022, the Kerala Police (KP) ordered 92 TriCa carbines.
According to OFT, the Greyhounds unit ordered 44 TARs.
In July 2022, the Government of Kerala received a request from KP to procure 250 TARs with side folding stocks.
The Government of Kerala received the TriCa carbines in May 2025.

According to the Advanced Weapons and Equipment India's (AWEIL) 2022–2023 Annual Report, the National Security Guard and the Andhra Pradesh Police conducted tests on both the TAR and the TriCa carbine.
In January 2023, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) received TARs manufactured from Rifle Factory Ishapore.
In April 2023, Minister of State for Defence and Tourism Ajay Bhatt visited OFT.
During his visit, Ajay Bhatt witnessed the TAR being manufactured in the factory.
Ajay Bhatt was briefed on OFT's research and development work.
In January 2024, BSF procured further TARs featuring bayonets.
The Government of Kerala published an approved plan for the KP to acquire 30 TARs.
In November 2023, the Trichy was on display at the Dasara Exhibition in Mysore, Karnataka as part of an effort to raise awareness on crime and public safety.
In a July 2024 interview, Rajesh Choudhary, Chairman and Managing Director of AWEIL, stated that the TAR continues to be in demand with CAPFs.
Rajesh Choudhary reported that an export order was made for the rifle.
In May 2025, it was reported that the Assam Forest Department and the Central Bureau of Narcotics made orders for the TriCa carbine.
Initial versions of the TAR were produced by using FN FAL-based receivers.
Initial versions of the TAR were using 7.62x39 mm magazines.
In 2012, there were reports that the prototypes jammed during testing.
The jamming was due to the rate of fire being 800 rounds per minute instead of 600 rounds per minute to match with the AK-47.
It was initially expected that the rate of fire would be at 650 rounds per minute.
The current version of the TAR is based on the AR-M1 with a machined receiver instead of stamped sheet.
The machined receiver ensures the rifle has high accuracy and reliability.
The TAR can be outfitted with picatinny rails on the upper handguard to attach scopes if requested.
In July 2021, it was reported that the TARs used by the Kerala Police are effective in Naxalite-Maoist counterinsurgency operations.
On August 2025, a TAR was secured from pro-Maoist communist Naxalite fighters in Chhattisgarh’s Narayanpur district.
The TAR can fire with single, burst and full automatic mode.
OFT reported that the TAR can be adopted with single shot mode only for police forces in cities and urban areas.
The TAR has an effective range of 300 to 350 metres.
The range of the TAR can be up to 500 metres if the rifle is used in full auto.
OFT claimed that the TAR is functionally on par with the AK-47.
The TAR can be equipped with several underbarrel grenade launchers, including the ARDE UBGL, the GP-25, the GP-30 and the Arsenal M6 UBGL.
The TAR can use bayonets.
Magazines for the TAR are supplied by Nilkamal Limited.
Magazines made for AK-47-based assault rifles can also be used with the TAR.
7.62×39 mm ammunition of all types can be used for the TAR.
The Trichy assault rifle is the main variant with a fixed stock.
The Trichy folding stock (side) is a TAR variant with a side folding stock.
The Trichy folding stock (down) is a TAR variant with a downfolding stock.
The Trichy folding stock (down) was unveiled on August 2021.
The Trichy folding stock (down) is sometimes referred to as a variant with an underfolding stock.
The Trichy Carbine (TriCa) was unveiled on January 2021.
The TriCa weights 3.17 kg.
The TriCa is marketed as a compact weapon for vehicle crews, paratroopers and special forces units.
The TriCA's firing range is from 150-175 metres.
A muzzle device is installed on the barrel of the TriCa to minimize muzzle flash and sound when it's fired.
The TriCa is a clone based on the Arsenal AR-M14SF.
The muzzle device of the TriCa is based on the AKS-74U.
The TriCa is sometimes known as Baby TAR or TAR-3.
The Border Security Force is a user of the TAR.
The Central Industrial Security Force is a user of the TAR.
The Central Reserve Police Force is a user of the TAR.
The Chhattisgarh Police is a user of the TAR.
The Greater Mumbai Police is a user of the TAR.
The Indo-Tibetan Border Police is a user of the TAR.
The Jharkhand Police is a user of the TAR.
The Kerala Police is a user of the TAR.
The Madhya Pradesh Police is a user of the TAR.
The National Security Guard is a user of the TAR.
The Rajasthan Police is a user of the TAR.
Rajesh Choudhary of AWEIL reported an export order from an unnamed country.
At least one Trichy was recovered from Naxalite guerrillas of the People's Liberation Guerrilla Army (India).
